correctness.rationale: Fix a marked outneighborhood of size d by exchangeability; the remaining orientation signs are independent symmetric Rademachers. The cyclic-triple indicator is a constant plus quadratic two-edge wedges; Q² survives only matching wedges, Q³ only three-star or triangle edge configurations with opposite signs, QL² only two crosscut edges sharing a vertex. This gives displayed cumulants exactly; differentiating (a+bq)/(v0+q/4)^(3/2) leaves b(m(m-1)/2-q)/8>0 for m≥4. Explicit direct orientation enumeration independently checked all marked degrees n=4..6. Limits n=4,n=5 and symmetry d↔m-d handled.

value.rationale: The cycle count is the canonical transitivity defect of a tournament. Exact finite-n score-conditioned third moments and the sharp balanced-degree skewness ordering reveal shape information not recoverable from existing mean/variance or unconditional subgraph-count asymptotics; they can inform finite-sample approximations.

final_claim: For independently fair tournaments n≥4, conditional on fixed marked degree d with m=n-1,N=binom(m,3),q=d(m-d): E C=N/4+q/2, Var C=3N/16+q/4, third central moment=3(4-m)N/32-3(m-2)q/16; from n≥6 all are negative and from n≥5 |standardized skewness| rises with q.
limitations: Fair independent edges, predetermined marked vertex, unordered cyclic triples only.
